newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu favoure multinational force - UN envoy.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu favoure multinational force - UN envoy.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko supports sending a multinational force to Zaire to help get relief to refugees and help them return home to Rwanda, a U.N. envoy said after meeting him on Wednesday.
Envoy Raymond Chretien quoted Mobutu as saying he would do his utmost to maintain calm in his country to let the multinational force work.

"President Mobutu told me Zaire would do everything possible to maintain this period of calm so that the multinational force discussed in Nairobi may be able to rapidly allow for food to reach refugees and help them return to their home countries, including of course Rwanda," Chretien said.
"He was very clear, very categorical," Chretien told reporters after the meeting at Mobutu's French Riviera villa.
He said the period of calm Mobutu mentioned referred to the unilateral ceasefire declared by Rwanda-backed Tutsi rebels fighting Zairean troops.
An eight-nation African summit in Nairobi on Tuesday called on the United Nations to send a "neutral" protection force to create havens from which refugees could go home along safe corridors.
